ideas.question: Has there been a change in maternal smoking rates among SUID cases from 2015 to 2019?
ideas.comparison: SUID cases in the NCFRP dataset from 2015 to 2019, compared with PRAMS population reference data for the same years.
ideas.why_open: While maternal smoking is a well-known risk factor for Sudden Unexpected Infant Death (SUID), trends over time may reflect changes in societal attitudes or intervention effectiveness. Understanding if smoking rates are declining can inform public health strategies to prevent SUID.
